terms.comment: Cicero’s definition: when the whole state is in one man’s hands, rēgem illum ūnum vocāmus (Rep. 1.42). After the last Tarquin was driven out the Romans hated the name; the word serves for the kings of every age and people. Also the king in chess and in cards (Traupman 51–52).

phrases.latin: Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre
phrases.english: At first the city of Rome was ruled by kings

phrases.latin: quī fuit rāna, nunc est rēx
phrases.english: the one who was a frog is now a king

sources: Lewis & Short: rex
